analysis:
Reviewed all 12 units; every change is test, tooling or test-harness only, with no production serving, auth, crypto or protocol code.

1) StartupPreloadTests.swift: a new test (failuresReachFailureHook) asserts the StartupPreloader onFailure hook receives load and self-test errors. The visible sections only exercise startup gate outcomes (disabled, warm, timedOut, cancelled), fail-closed retirement with re-registration, and no-evict load admission. The tests use local stubs and an in-process mock coordinator. makeFakeHFSnapshot writes under the real HF cache and cleans up with defer, which is a test hygiene matter, not a security one. These tests reinforce that fail-closed self-test retirement removes a model from the advertised set (relevant to T-008/T-027). I did not see the production code, so the onFailure hook's logging behavior is unverified; if it logs error text derived from model paths or prompts, that is a question for the production change reviewers.

2) scripts/benchmarks/glm_load_timeline.py (+ test): offline log parser, run locally by the operator. It reads a local file with regexes, with no network, subprocess, eval or untrusted deserialization. The regexes are simple with no obvious catastrophic backtracking. It writes JSON only to a user-specified path. It references log lines indicating that weight-hash verification may be 'reused' from a prior full verification, while the GLM load re-verifies all manifest files with SHA-256 before serving. That production behavior (a verified-weights record file, DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE) is not in the supplied evidence. Integration should check, outside this batch, that the recorded hash cache cannot be used to skip verification of changed weights (T-012/T-027). The log text says file identities are checked and the load verifies again.

3) scripts/run-provider-tests.sh: adds an export of DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE pointing into the mktemp -d test root, which is cleaned up by trap. It isolates tests from the operator's real verified-weights record, a positive hygiene change. mktemp -d creates a private 0700 directory.

No security regressions found in this batch. The remaining open question is the unseen production implementation of the verified-weights record and the weight-verification path.
